samples: This is a pure calculation library (no files, network or console) for invoices made of lines, each with a description, a quantity of at least 1 and a non-negative unit price, plus a customer name and a discount percentage that must be between 0 and 100. It can price a single line, sum all lines into a subtotal, and produce a final total with the percentage discount taken off and the result rounded to two decimal places, using exact decimal arithmetic rather than floats. It does not handle tax, shipping, currencies or storage, and its two tests cover only a 10% discount and an empty invoice, so check the rounding behavior yourself if you need a specific rule for half-cent cases.

This is a pure, side-effect-free invoice library: it models lines (description, quantity, unit price) and invoices (customer, lines, discount percentage), then computes each line's total, the invoice subtotal, and the final total after the percentage discount, rounded to two decimal places. Construction enforces the business rules (quantity of at least 1, non-negative prices, discount between 0 and 100), and it uses exact decimal arithmetic, so it suits money. Two caveats: the rounding rule is whatever the library's rounding does (the code doesn't spell it out), and one test compares the total of an empty invoice to a bare integer zero, which may be flagged as a type mismatch if the checker is strict about mixing integer and decimal values.

This module calculates what a customer owes: each line is quantity times unit price, the subtotal adds up the lines, and the total subtracts a percentage discount and rounds to cents using exact decimal arithmetic rather than floating point. The types reject bad data when records are built (quantity below 1, negative prices, or a discount outside 0 to 100 percent), so the functions never see such input. It is pure, with no file, network, or console access, so it is safe to embed, though it covers only this one discount style, with no tax, currency, or per-line discounts.

This module computes invoice amounts: each line is quantity times unit price, the subtotal is the sum of the lines, and the total applies the invoice's percentage discount and rounds to two decimal places. It uses exact decimal arithmetic rather than floats, and the types reject invalid data, such as a quantity below 1, a negative price, or a discount outside 0 to 100 percent. The functions are pure, with no file, network or other side effects, so they are safe to call anywhere, but it handles only a single percentage discount and does not cover tax, currencies, or any rounding rule beyond what the library's rounding does by default.

This module models an invoice as a customer plus a list of lines, each with a description, a quantity of at least 1 and a non-negative unit price, and a discount percentage limited to 0-100. It can compute each line's total, the subtotal of all lines, and a final total in which the percentage discount is taken from the whole subtotal and the result is rounded to cents only once, at the end. It is pure calculation with no I/O or side effects, and the bad-input checks are built into the types. The included tests cover only a ten percent discount and an empty invoice, so other rounding cases are not shown.
